chronology.bounds_fitted_on: the clean bodies of the sample, never on the transformed set

findings.consequence: a sealed v2 feature vector is reproducible from its candidate source, the fitting bounds *and the exact batch it was encoded in*. The first two alone are not enough, and any check that re-encodes under different batching will disagree with the seal
findings.detail: the frozen MiniLM is batch-composition dependent. The same text embedded on its own and embedded alongside a longer sequence differ, because the shorter one is padded to the batch's length. The difference is around 1e-7 -- invisible to a cosine, fatal to a hash
findings.found_by: the first run of this regression, which reported 62 changed vectors including 7 for a case that does not touch the candidate source
findings.how_this_record_avoids_it: every source here is embedded window by window on its own, so a difference between a clean and a transformed vector can only come from the transformation

measured.how: the same text embedded on its own, then as the second member of a batch whose first member is longer, so it is padded to the longer length

findings.what_it_does_not_invalidate: the seals themselves, which are records of the bytes that were actually encoded, and every scan and threshold that compares vectors by distance rather than by hash

findings.correction: read that field as 're-seals identically from the same encoded records'. Given W2-D9 the stronger claim its name makes is false: re-embedding under different batching would not reproduce the seal
findings.detail: sprint-21d4-feature-seals.json reports `reencodes_identically_from_source_alone: true` for both partitions. The check behind it re-ran the sealing function over the same PendingFeatureV2 records, which already carry their embeddings, so it never re-embedded anything. It proves the sealing function is deterministic given identical inputs, which is worth knowing and is not what the field name says
findings.found_by: reading S21D4-034's re-encode proof while investigating W2-D9

first_action.reading: with no fitted ranker in force the first action is the head of the baseline order; this compares the body the system would act on first by its canonical identity. The ranker-dependent form belongs to S21D4-039

independence.reading: 160 transformed candidate vectors, every one identical to its clean counterpart, so the forty transformed decisions repeat twenty clean ones and add none. This is the number S21D4-032 sealed as zero and the property the regression tests

purpose: execute the claim S21D4-032 sealed: a transformation repeats its source group's fitted feature vector, so it adds no independent decision

semantic_mutation_control.why: the invariance result above says a rename does not move the canonical bytes. This says a changed meaning does. Without it, a canonicaliser that mapped every program to one value would satisfy the first claim completely

verifier.how: plain pytest in a scratch directory. A precheck that wrote governed outcomes would put transformed rows in the store the clean campaign owns
